rationale_evidence.statement: Analyzes whether the necessity-half minimality claim (C) depends on the commissioned falsification: its evidential basis (artifact D SS3, 19:24) pre-dates the commission by 35 minutes, so C does not need the falsification for an executed basis -- but artifact D is self-administered (same reconstruction defines and tests K), so the commission's claimed INDEPENDENT check was never actually performed as commissioned; when independent parties did later attack (20:47, 21:05, 21:13), all three found something wrong, two of which still stand. rationale_evidence.anchor: Falsification ≠ minimality ... falsification found ⇒ minimality false: No ... removal test passed ⇒ Minimality(K|𝒯): Yes, and only that ... Minimality(K|𝒯) ⇒ K is the kernel: No
rationale_evidence.statement: Applies the commission's own existential/asymmetric falsification criterion strictly: finding a falsification does NOT imply minimality is false (the counterexamples attack sufficiency E, not necessity C); absence of falsification does NOT imply minimality is true (forbidden by the commission itself); a passed removal test implies ONLY type-A Minimality(K|T) relative to an enumerated T over an assumed-complete capability list; and Minimality(K|T) does NOT imply K is the kernel ('A is not evidence for B, C or D', per THEORY-COMPLETION-GAP-REGISTER SS2). Concludes the commissioned test, even if run and passed, could never have established C, D, or F -- only raised confidence in E.
